title: Pediatric Hip Pathology: SCFE, Legg-Calve-Perthes and Synovitis

steps.say: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis occurs in overweight adolescents during their rapid growth spurt. A type one Salter-Harris fracture through the hypertrophic zone causes the displacement.
steps.tx: Recognize **SCFE age and demographics** when adolescents present with hip, groin, thigh, or knee pain. Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) is a Salter-Harris Type I physeal fracture through the hypertrophic zone of the proximal femoral physis. It occurs predominantly in overweight adolescents (males 12-14 years, females 10-12 years), who frequently present with referred medial knee pain that delays hip imaging (Klein line criteria).

rows: Failure to suspect SCFE in atypical ages
May be triggered by endocrinopathy if thin
Referred pain to thigh or knee
Ordering knee x-rays while ignoring the hip

steps.say: On anteroposterior and frog-leg lateral pelvic radiographs, clinicians assess the Klein line along the superior femoral neck. Failure of this line to intersect the lateral epiphysis indicates Trethowan sign.
steps.tx: Evaluate the **Klein line criteria** on AP and frog-leg lateral pelvic radiographs. A line drawn tangential to the superior border of the femoral neck (Klein line) should normally intersect the lateral aspect of the capital femoral epiphysis. In SCFE, the slipped epiphysis fails to intersect the line, a finding known as Trethowan sign. Bilateral frog-leg lateral views provide the highest sensitivity for detecting subtle early slips (Slip direction).

steps.say: The capital femoral epiphysis slips posteromedially relative to the neck, resembling a scoop of ice cream falling off a cone. The femoral neck actually shifts anterolaterally.
steps.tx: Understand the **posteromedial slip direction** biomechanics in SCFE. While the terminology implies epiphyseal movement, the capital femoral epiphysis remains firmly anchored within the acetabulum by the ligamentum teres while the femoral neck displaces anterosuperiorly and rotates externally. On radiographs, this creates the classic appearance of a scoop of ice cream slipping posteromedially off its cone (Bilateral risk).

nodes.label: Axial shear stress on weakened growth plate

steps.say: Bilateral slipped capital femoral epiphysis is remarkably common, affecting up to forty percent of patients. If a child has hypothyroidism or renal osteodystrophy, the bilateral risk exceeds fifty percent.
steps.tx: Screen for **bilateral involvement in SCFE** in every diagnosed patient. Bilateral slips occur in 20-40% of cases, presenting either simultaneously or sequentially within 12 to 18 months. If an underlying endocrinopathy exists (hypothyroidism, growth hormone deficiency, renal osteodystrophy), the bilateral rate exceeds 50%, prompting many pediatric orthopedists to perform prophylactic contralateral in-situ screw fixation (Perthes disease).

rows: Close serial frog-leg radiographs or pinning

steps.say: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease is idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head in young children. Active boys aged four to eight years present with a painless or low-grade limp.
steps.tx: Recognize **Legg-Calve-Perthes disease peak age** and presentation. Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (LCPD) is idiopathic avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis occurring in children aged 4 to 8 years, with a marked 4:1 male-to-female predominance. Children typically present with an unprovoked, painless or mildly aching limp and insidious loss of internal rotation and abduction of the hip (Waldenstrom staging).

steps.say: Perthes disease progresses through four distinct radiographic stages described by Waldenstrom. An early subchondral crescent fracture gives way to fragmentation and subsequent reossification.
steps.tx: Trace the **Waldenstrom radiographic stages** of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease across disease evolution. Stage 1 (Initial) manifests as femoral head sclerosis, joint space widening, and a subchondral fracture (crescent sign). Stage 2 (Fragmentation) features epiphyseal collapse and radiolucent fissuring. Stage 3 (Reossification) shows gradual restoration of bone density, leading to Stage 4 (Remodeling) with healed spherical or flattened head morphology (Herring classification).

nodes.label: Stage 3 (Reossification): New bone fills avascular zone
Stage 4 (Remodeling): Healed spherical or aspherical head

steps.say: The Herring lateral pillar classification determines long-term prognosis during the fragmentation stage. Maintaining over fifty percent of the lateral pillar height protects against late osteoarthritis.
steps.tx: Apply the **Catterall and Herring classifications** during the fragmentation stage of Perthes disease. The Herring lateral pillar classification on AP pelvis radiographs provides the most accurate prognostic guide: Group A maintains 100% lateral pillar height (excellent prognosis); Group B maintains > 50% height (favorable outcome); and Group C suffers > 50% loss of lateral pillar height, resulting in femoral head deformity and early osteoarthritis (Transient synovitis).

steps.say: Transient synovitis is a benign, self-limiting hip effusion following a mild viral illness. Pelvic radiographs are normal, and ultrasound confirms an effusion that resolves within days.
steps.tx: Differentiate **transient synovitis ultrasound** findings from septic arthritis. Transient synovitis (toxic synovitis) is a self-limiting, post-viral inflammatory effusion occurring in children aged 3-8 years. Pelvic radiographs are normal without bone destruction, while ultrasound demonstrates a small-to-moderate hip effusion that resolves completely within 7-10 days with rest and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory therapy.
